sampling_model.design: A fixed two-block panel with deterministic factors, an untreated pre block, a treated post block, and Gaussian sampling noise.
sampling_model.units: All \(N\) labeled units are observed in every one of the \(T_0+T_1\) periods; \(N,r,s\) are fixed and known.
sampling_model.treatment: The realized intervention switches on after the break, and \(\beta_i\) is the time-averaged attributable contrast for labeled unit \(i\).
sampling_model.overlap: No assignment-overlap condition is invoked because treatment timing is fixed; identification is governed by \(\kappa_s(L)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The loading projector is inferred from \(T_0^{-1}Y_0Y_0^{\top}\); all procedures may use the full panel, and no subspace rate is assumed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: We propose consistent and asymptotically normal estimation and establish statistical inference for the direct and interference effects averaged over post-intervention periods.

body.tldr: For the displayed nonempty Gaussian panel class with ordered loading and noise bounds and \(K\ge\sqrt r\), sparse direct and spillover effects are decoded from a post-period mean through a loading subspace learned from the untreated pre-panel. The proved results are a finite-sample globally honest confidence set with a sharp global-honesty expected-diameter frontier, equality of global and margin-oracle rates throughout the weak-margin region, and a maximal-margin adaptation gain in the \(N=3,r=s=1\) experiment once an explicit four-line classifier has error at most \(\alpha/2\). The same-sample oracle characterization over the remaining nonempty margin strata is not proved: disconnected loading components and finite classification transitions remain the central open question.

project_justification.gap: HeLiShiMiao2026 turns panel interference into sparse robust regression but relies on a majority-valid-controls count, asymptotic selection, and coordinatewise inference. Sparse-confidence theory assumes an observed design, while projector-confidence theory does not propagate geometry into a causal sparse-vector diameter frontier. No opened paper characterizes global-versus-margin-oracle honest diameter when the loading operator is estimated from the same fixed-factor panel.
project_justification.niche: The exact Gaussian subclass makes the two information channels visible: post-period noise perturbs the sparse decomposition, and pre-period noise perturbs the loading geometry. Constant post factors force lower bounds to pay for geometry only through the original pre observations, while maximal-margin strata may split into finitely classifiable components.
project_justification.fill: The project combines an exact pre-panel second-moment region based only on the signal-versus-noise gap, finite support enumeration, every-sample diameter control, compensated-rotation lower bounds, and component-aware Gaussian decision inversion. On every nonempty primitive class it delivers the adaptive frontier, the weak-margin oracle equivalence, and a rank-one maximal-margin result from an explicit four-hypothesis experiment; the finite same-sample oracle profile on intermediate nonempty margins remains the open kernel.

body.related_work: HeLiShiMiao2026, Introduction, Assumptions 1--4, Theorem 1, its proof, and Discussion, moves from contaminated donors to a factor-adjusted sparse outlier vector and applied direct-and-spillover targets. The displayed class here is not their Assumptions 1--4 class, and neither class contains the other: this paper imposes homoskedastic independent Gaussian errors, exact centered and normalized bounded deterministic factors, constant post-period effects, and bounded latent means and effects, while it drops their distinct-loading-strength and majority-valid-controls requirements. Its proved global frontier, weak-margin oracle equivalence, and thresholded rank-one endpoint therefore apply only to the displayed class and do not transfer to the full He--Li--Shi--Miao class by inclusion. Wei2026, Sections 3--4, Lemma 1, Theorem 1, Theorem 2, and Conclusion, gives donor-classification-free sharp scalar partial identification by full-simplex reduction and Farkas certificates in a different envelope model; it informs the finite inversion architecture but is not a comparator the present point-identified model claims to tighten. NicklVanDeGeer2013, Theorems 3--5 and their testing reduction, and CaiGuo2017 supply composite-mixture lower-bound logic for sparse confidence procedures with observed random designs. CaiLow2004 supplies the ordered-modulus view of subclass-versus-union expected length, while EvansHansenStark2005 supplies confidence-set decision duality; neither identifies the four nuisance-profiled Gaussian loading hypotheses nor the pathwise post-inversion diameter used at the maximal rank-one margin. NaumovSpokoinyUlyanov2017, Theorem 1 and its Gaussian comparison proof, supplies the projector-region exemplar, but its i.i.d. covariance experiment differs from the deterministic normalized factor panel; here the relevant eigengap is only the \(d_{\mathrm{lo}}^2\) separation between the signal subspace and noise, so repeated nonzero loading strengths are allowed. ChandrasekaranEtAl2011 and FickusMixon2013 own the generic sparse-subspace and erasure-robust geometry, so the uniqueness lemma is supporting rather than headline novelty. GoffMbakop2026 shows how estimated linear-system solvability can be tested uniformly, but its coefficient regularity does not solve the OPEN disconnected same-sample all-margin oracle problem.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The general oracle step is not established by the available modulus sandwich: upper and lower bounds evaluate sparse-compatible subspace moduli at different resolution constants, and that mismatch is material when a new loading component becomes statistically reachable. The explicit four-line result settles only \(\gamma=1/\sqrt3\) when \(T_0\ge\overline T\); short-pre-panel classification and all intermediate high-margin profiles remain part of the open question. In the bounded \(N=8,r=2,s=3\) kill test, direct enumeration reproduced \(\kappa_3=0.06586041095768684\) for the polynomial frame, and a seeded search over 200000 Gaussian-QR frames found margin \(0.09652308016949927\). The latter is only a numerical lower bound on \(\kappa_\star\), not a certificate of maximality or of its component geometry, so it cannot determine the same-sample oracle transition.
body.honest_scope: The displayed class is a separate homoskedastic Gaussian specialization of the fixed-factor panel problem, with fixed \(N,r,s\), unknown deterministic factors, \(T_0\ge r+1\), ordered primitive bounds \(d_{\mathrm{lo}}\le d_{\mathrm{hi}}\) and \(\sigma_{\mathrm{lo}}\le\sigma_{\mathrm{hi}}\), and \(K\ge\sqrt r\). It is not the HeLiShiMiao2026 Assumptions 1--4 class, and no class inclusion transfers the theorems: this class is narrower through homoskedastic independent Gaussian errors, exact centered and normalized bounded deterministic factors, constant post-period effects, and bounded latent means and effects, but relaxes their distinct-loading-strength and majority-valid-controls requirements. Every theorem here is restricted to the displayed class. Every global-honesty and minimax-risk claim is conditional on \(\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(0)\ne\varnothing\), and every margin-specific claim is additionally restricted to nonempty \(\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(\gamma)\). The deterministic sparse-decomposition equivalence holds for every \(L\in\operatorname{Gr}(r,N)\), whether or not that subspace is realized by the panel model. Only its complete-observed-law converse is conditioned on realization: if a zero-margin \(L\) is the loading space of an admissible member, two legal effect vectors with constant post factors and common pre parameters generate the same full law. Repeated loading strengths are allowed because projector control uses only the \(d_{\mathrm{lo}}^2\) signal-versus-noise gap. There is no post-factor covariance lower bound, beta-min condition, correct-support event, or oracle subspace. The proved scope consists of the global adaptive frontier, weak-margin oracle equivalence, and the \(N=3,r=s=1\) maximal-margin endpoint after the explicit classifier fits inside the reserved noncoverage budget. The same-sample all-margin oracle profile, including intermediate and short-\(T_0\) component transitions, remains OPEN.
